title: The Book of the Prophet Isaiah, Chapters XL–LXVI (Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges)

verification_log.method: pp. xv–xvii: the first modern challenge to Isaianic authorship was Döderlein (1775), with Ibn Ezra a guarded forerunner; since Delitzsch (1890) an exilic author is "the unanimous verdict of Old Testament scholarship", on historical, conceptual and stylistic grounds; pp. xxxiii–xl: Cyrus is already a famous conqueror but Babylon not yet taken, so chs. 40–48 date between 550 and 539, "almost certainly after 546"
